frequency_restriction: Restrict underground-style high-frequency taiban scheduling; major-scale work should use releases, online signing, concerts, media and goods rather than 20+ small lives.
staff_meeting_signal: Strong cash efficiency if release/signing/goods calendar is healthy; watch large production and venue commitments.
member_meeting_signal: Members can support major activity if recovery and individual work are protected; avoid treating stable roster as replaceable.
fan_survey_signal: Fans value stable member attachment, high-quality releases, concerts and transparent graduation handling.
main_gameplay_risk: Overloading a fixed roster or damaging accumulated member/IP trust.

frequency_restriction: Restrict cheki/live-grind strategies; frequency should be release, tour, media and generation-event driven.
staff_meeting_signal: Succession planning, selection balance and brand continuity matter more than small-event volume.
member_meeting_signal: Senior/new generation balance is sensitive; too-fast pushes or too-slow integration both create morale risk.
fan_survey_signal: Fans expect institutional continuity but react strongly to selection, center and graduation handling.
main_gameplay_risk: Failed succession, fan split between generations, or brand dilution.

frequency_restriction: Allow aggressive frequency but cap by average condition, minor/student load, absence rate and staff capacity.
staff_meeting_signal: Cash and fan-contact opportunities rise quickly, but staff load and event conflicts become severe.
member_meeting_signal: Members may accept the push while momentum is strong, but fatigue and absence risk compound sharply.
fan_survey_signal: Fans want frequent lives and post-live tokutenkai chances; demand may exceed member service capacity.
main_gameplay_risk: Overextension, illness/absence spiral, turnover, and internal ecosystem crowding.

frequency_restriction: Do not solve only by adding lives; require online/release-event benefit access, member-content work and merchandise readiness.
staff_meeting_signal: Awareness is valuable but conversion leaks if online/physical benefit access, merch and repeat-live pathways are weak.
member_meeting_signal: Members need more identity-building chances, not just song/content reach; avoid hollow exposure.
fan_survey_signal: Casual listeners know songs, while core fans ask for clearer ways to attach to members and spend.
main_gameplay_risk: High awareness without durable repeat attendance, oshi attachment and spending.

frequency_restriction: Allow moderate-high underground frequency, but cap if utilization is low or condition declines; avoid prestige overreach too early.
staff_meeting_signal: Short-term cash needs live/post-live tokutenkai activity, but rebuilding mature member-specific demand takes months.
member_meeting_signal: Veterans need recognition; newer members need staged exposure and protection from weak early queues.
fan_survey_signal: Fans retain history attachment but do not automatically transfer oshi equity to replacements.
main_gameplay_risk: Decline spiral from lost member equity, weak new-member queues and league/event underperformance.

frequency_restriction: Allow high professional-underground activity, but one-man milestones should consume prep/recovery budget.
staff_meeting_signal: Direct fan economy can fund ambition even when CD sales are not a strong proxy.
member_meeting_signal: Members gain from strong live identity, but post-milestone roster shocks need recovery and trust handling.
fan_survey_signal: Core fans respond to lives, merch, post-live tokutenkai and birthday events more than mass viral reach.
main_gameplay_risk: Mistaking weak CD sales for weak business, or mishandling post-milestone roster changes.

frequency_restriction: Frequency should stay moderate during reboot; protect off-days and trust while rebuilding demand.
staff_meeting_signal: The reboot story can attract attention, but professionalism and operational discipline must support it.
member_meeting_signal: Members with prior careers need belief, safety and clear role promises; avoid chaotic overpush.
fan_survey_signal: Fans can buy into the revival narrative if management feels sincere and stable.
main_gameplay_risk: Trust collapse from producer overreach, unclear boundaries or another failed reboot.
